bio.en: Christina Wodtke is a multi-time author, Stanford lecturer (product management, game design), and consultant who specializes in OKRs and product development processes, with product leadership experience at LinkedIn, MySpace, Zynga, and Yahoo.
bio.zh: Christina Wodtke 是多次著书者、斯坦福讲师（产品管理、游戏设计）和顾问，专长于 OKR 与产品开发流程，曾在 LinkedIn、MySpace、Zynga 和 Yahoo 担任产品领导。

summary.en: Christina goes deep into OKRs—the atomic unit of an objective, what's commonly broken about OKR processes, and how the best companies leverage them. She covers the elements of a healthy OKR cadence, how OKRs fit with mission, vision, strategy, and roadmaps, and the often-overlooked power of celebration. The conversation also touches on storytelling and her most contrarian advice for new PMs.

What's the most awesome thing that happened in marketing? What's the most awesome thing that design did this week?" It makes people feel like they're part of something really special, and it's super exciting.

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: I've seen so many companies do extremely well with it, and I would say that not all companies will be successful, period. Companies are really successful with it are companies that... I think I can swear a little, they have their shit together.
turns.zh: 我见过很多公司在这方面做得非常好，但我想说的是，并不是所有公司都会成功。真正在这方面取得成功的公司是……我想我可以发誓，他们有自己的一套。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely. 100%.

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: And the first step is, get your shit together. They have strategy, they have empowered teams, they have psychological safety, and then the OKRs are that extra layer that supercharges them. So, I say OKRs are more of a vitamin, they're not a medicine. So, if you take OKRs and you're like, "Oh, this will fix everything that's wrong with you." No, that's not going to happen. It's just going to reveal everything that's wrong with your company. But if you've done the hard work of getting your company to be strong, it's amazing how well it works. It works really well with startups. It works really well with multidisciplinary product teams. I've seen it over and over. I don't really have permission to talk about all my clients, but I have one client that I'm just working with right now, and it's a purpose built company. So, in other words, they exist in order to make the lives of their customers better, healthier, wellness. (00:06:20): And so, they used OKRs to really create this amazing focus on, what does it mean to make everybody's life healthier? And one thing that came out of applying OKRs was this wonderful idea, they're bringing robots into their warehouses, not to replace their humans, they're keeping all the humans, but to reduce the amount of back problems their humans have. So, the humans are doing much more complex tasks, thinking about inventory and how to be more efficient. And the robots are doing the heavy lifting. (00:06:51): They've been growing and growing like crazy. And the OKRs are this very simple way of allowing you to focus on what actually matters and making sure you don't forget in the chaos of everyday life. So, if you know what you're trying to do, then the OKRs just help that happen. It aligns the company. And I think they're a lot like dieting advice, in that they say, "Eat less and exercise more." Well, that's really simple. It's worked for me. I've lost 25 pounds doing eat less and exercise more. But wow, it's hard. It's really hard to do. And I think about OKRs that way. You have to just stay with it and be strong and committed, and that will help.
turns.zh: 第一步是，整理好你的东西。他们有策略，他们有授权的团队，他们有心理安全感，然后 OKR 就是给他们增压的额外层。所以，我说 OKR 更像是一种维生素，而不是一种药物。所以，如果你采用 OKR，你会想，“哦，这会解决你所有的问题。”不，那不会发生。它只会揭露你公司的所有问题。但如果你付出了艰苦的努力让你的公司变得强大，那么它的运作效果会令人惊讶。它非常适合初创公司。它与多学科产品团队配合得非常好。我已经看过一遍又一遍了。我实际上没有权限谈论我的所有客户，但我现在正在与一个客户合作，这是一家专门建立的公司。所以，换句话说，它们的存在是为了让顾客的生活变得更好、更健康、更幸福。 (00:06:20)：因此，他们使用 OKR 真正创造了这一令人惊叹的焦点：让每个人的生活更健康意味着什么？应用 OKR 产生的一件事是这个绝妙的想法，他们将机器人带入仓库，不是为了取代人类，而是保留所有人类，而是为了减少人类的背部问题。因此，人类正在执行更复杂的任务，思考库存以及如何提高效率。机器人正在承担繁重的工作。 (00:06:51)：他们一直在疯狂地成长。 OKR 是一种非常简单的方法，可以让您专注于真正重要的事情，并确保您不会在日常生活的混乱中忘记。因此，如果您知道自己想要做什么，那么 OKR 就会帮助您实现这一目标。它使公司保持一致。我认为它们很像节食建议，因为他们说“少吃多运动”。嗯，这真的很简单。这对我有用。通过少吃多运动，我的体重减轻了 25 磅。但是哇，这很难。确实很难做到。我也是这样考虑 OKR 的。你必须坚持下去，坚强并坚定，这会有帮助。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, I'll start with, you talked about the benefits of OKR. If you had to just boil down, here's what OKRs can do for you as a company, as an organization, what would that be? What's just the main benefit of OKRs at your company?
turns.zh: 那么，我首先，您谈到了 OKR 的好处。如果您必须归结为以下几点，那么 OKR 可以为您作为一家公司、一个组织做些什么，那会是什么？ OKR 在贵公司的主要好处是什么？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: The main benefit is that there's a lot of concrete action through a OKR that you don't always get from strategy. Strategy tends to be a little longer, a little more Muji Muji. And then when you get the OKR, you say, "This quarter is what we're actually going to be doing, and these are the numbers we're actually going to be pushing further." So, that's really good. It creates a cadence of progress, which is incredibly valuable. It creates alignment. There's no question what the single most important thing to do in the company is, assuming you're doing radical focus and you don't have 20 OKRs every quarter. Ugh, don't like to think about that. And last of all, the thing that I don't see a lot of people talking about that I think is really amazing, is because an OKR focuses you for one quarter and at the end of the quarter you grade your OKRs. (00:08:40): How well did we do? What got in our way? It creates this learning cycle. So, then you can take that information and say, "Next quarter, what should we try next?" And I think the time is the thing that a lot of leaders really struggle to think about. But if you've been really focusing on say, retention for one quarter, two quarters, and then you go over and say, "Okay, let's work on acquisition." You don't forget all the things you learned about retention. No, you're just building knowledge and building knowledge and building knowledge, which means your company will constantly get smarter and more effective.
turns.zh: 主要好处是，通过 OKR 可以采取很多具体行动，而这些行动并不总是从战略中获得。策略往往会长一点，无印良品一点。然后，当您获得 OKR 时，您会说：“本季度是我们实际上要做的事情，这些是我们实际上要进一步推动的数字。”所以，这真的很好。它创造了一种进步的节奏，这是非常有价值的。它创建对齐。毫无疑问，在公司里最重要的事情是什么，假设你正在做彻底的专注，并且每个季度没有 20 个 OKR。呃，不喜欢去想这个。最后，我没有看到很多人谈论我认为真正令人惊奇的事情，因为 OKR 让你专注于一个季度，并在季度末对你的 OKR 进行评分。 (00:08:40)：我们做得怎么样？是什么阻碍了我们？它创造了这个学习周期。因此，您可以利用该信息并说：“下个季度，我们接下来应该尝试什么？”我认为时间是很多领导者真正难以思考的问题。但如果你真的专注于一个季度、两个季度的保留，然后你会说：“好吧，让我们开始收购。”您不会忘记您学到的有关保留的所有知识。不，你只是在积累知识、积累知识、积累知识，这意味着你的公司将不断变得更智能、更高效。

turns.speaker: Lenny

And maybe a simple way to think about it is, it's like a plug-and-play product development process. You don't have to invent everything from scratch. There's this thing that exists. I know it's not the whole piece of it, but yeah, maybe... You're nodding and I'm curious, when I say that, what comes to mind?

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Yeah, I guess you have to have a product development process, because obviously otherwise you're just running around chickens with your heads cut off, but it keeps you from making the same stupid mistake over and over and over again, which has been a goal in my life. My motto is, "Make new mistakes." So, by having this focus on really important things, not to spread yourself too thin, like the famous peanut butter memo from Yahoo, which I guess was long ago enough, not everybody remembers it. But companies have a tendency to try to do everything all at this exact moment. And so, everybody's working with 1% on this, 1% on that and 1% on the other. And instead you use the OKRs and say, "Okay, this is the big rock we're going to move. This is the big thing that's going to happen this quarter, and you can fiddle around with all the other stuff if you want, but this one has to move." (00:10:27): And then the next quarter, the next thing gets moved and so on. And it just accelerates the speed of your accomplishments so much. It's kind of mind-blowing. I've actually been running my life for the last eight, 10 years on OKRs as well because I'm ADHD and I'm all over the place. And so, looking at my OKRs every single Monday and saying, "Well, am I going to work on a book? Am I going to work on my teaching? Am I going to work... Where do I want to put that attention?" It changes me personally, just like it changes my clients.
turns.zh: 是的，我想你必须有一个产品开发流程，因为显然否则你只是在被砍掉头的鸡周围跑，但它可以让你避免一遍又一遍地犯同样的愚蠢错误，这一直是我一生的目标。我的座右铭是“犯新错误”。因此，通过将注意力集中在真正重要的事情上，不要让自己太分散，就像雅虎著名的花生酱备忘录一样，我想这已经是很久以前的事了，并不是每个人都记得它。但公司倾向于在此时此刻把所有事情都做完。因此，每个人都在这个上投入 1%，在那个上投入 1%，在另一个上投入 1%。相反，你使用 OKR 并说：“好吧，这是我们要移动的大石头。这是本季度将发生的大事，如果你愿意，你可以摆弄所有其他东西，但这个必须移动。” (00:10:27)：然后下个季度，下一个事情就会发生变化，依此类推。它只会大大加快你取得成就的速度。这有点令人兴奋。事实上，在过去的八年、十年里，我一直在按照 OKR 来管理我的生活，因为我患有注意力缺陷多动症，而且我的生活到处都是。因此，每周一查看我的 OKR 并说：“好吧，我要写一本书吗？我要继续教学吗？我要工作吗……我想把注意力放在哪里？”它改变了我个人，就像它改变了我的客户一样。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's an example of your personal care? You said writing a book maybe could be one?
turns.zh: 您的个人护理的例子是什么？你说写一本书也许是其中之一？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Well, I wish, but no, it's actually been health. One of the great things about managing my OKRs for so long is I discovered this pattern, which is that anytime things get busy, I just stop taking care of myself completely. And that's really bad because if I'm healthy, I can be there for my kid, I can be there for my students, I can be there for my colleagues. So, this quarter's been about setting up habits of well-being and like I said, I've been really pleased at how it's been going.
turns.zh: 嗯，我希望，但不，这实际上是健康。长期管理 OKR 的好处之一是我发现了这种模式，即每当事情变得忙碌时，我就会完全不再照顾自己。这真的很糟糕，因为如果我身体健康，我就可以陪伴我的孩子，我可以陪伴我的学生，我可以陪伴我的同事。所以，这个季度的重点是建立幸福的习惯，就像我说的，我对它的进展感到非常满意。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. I haven't heard that before. What would you say is kind of the atomic unit of an OKR? So, people talk about, "We're doing OKRs, we're not doing OKRs". What's the line between we have goals and a plan, and we're actually doing OKRs as a concept?
turns.zh: 惊人的。我以前没听说过。您认为 OKR 的原子单元是什么？因此，人们谈论“我们正在做 OKR，我们没有做 OKR”。我们的目标和计划与我们实际上将 OKR 作为一个概念来执行之间的界限是什么？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Gosh, what is the atomic unit? That's a really lovely question. I would say, "What am I doing this week to get closer to our goals?" If you could answer that question, you could give up all the OKR stuff, but if you just asked the question, "What are we doing this week to get closer to our strategic goals, our longer term goals?" That is the very heart of it, because there's the tomorrow problem, like my kid will do his homework tomorrow, and tomorrow never comes. It's always tomorrow, tomorrow, tomorrow. So, what are we doing right now? And I find that it's really useful to tie it into temporal landmarks. (00:12:21): By that I mean that there are things like birthdays or New Year's or Mondays or quarters that are already built into the world. And so, we piggyback onto them and we say, "Okay, it's Q1, boom, we're going to stop. We're going to take a breath, we're going to look at everything and we're going to say, 'What do we actually have to do?'" Raising your head above the noise is really vital. "And then this quarter, remember we have a mission over here and we have a vision and we have a strategy. Okay, this quarter's all about, what?" And you move towards that. (00:12:52): I know there's a lot of talk about outcomes and I think that's absolutely right. It's really critical to think about outcomes because that gives you flexibility on how to attack the problem. But the biggest question is, why? Why do we get up in the morning? What are we trying to actually do? Are we making a difference at all? And if you can say, "This week I'm going to do this," and then at the end of the week you say, "Oh, that worked or that didn't work," and you can try something new or keep going. That's just invaluable.
turns.zh: 天哪，原子单位是什么？这是一个非常可爱的问题。我会说，“这周我要做什么才能更接近我们的目标？”如果你能回答这个问题，你就可以放弃所有 OKR 的东西，但如果你只是问这个问题，“我们本周要做什么来更接近我们的战略目标，我们的长期目标？”这就是它的核心，因为存在明天的问题，就像我的孩子明天要做作业，但明天永远不会到来。永远都是明天、明天、明天。那么，我们现在在做什么？我发现将其与时间地标联系起来确实很有用。 (00:12:21)：我的意思是，生日、新年、星期一或季度等事情已经内置于世界中。所以，我们背着他们说，“好吧，现在是第一季度，繁荣，我们要停下来了。我们要喘口气，我们要看看一切，我们要说，‘我们实际上必须做什么？’”抬起头来超越噪音真的很重要。 “然后这个季度，请记住我们在这里有一个使命，我们有一个愿景，我们有一个战略。好吧，这个季度的重点是什么？”然后你就朝着这个方向前进。 (00:12:52)：我知道有很多关于结果的讨论，我认为这是绝对正确的。考虑结果非常重要，因为这可以让您灵活地解决问题。但最大的问题是，为什么？我们为什么早上起床？我们实际上想做什么？我们真的有所作为吗？如果你可以说，“这周我要做这个”，然后在周末你说，“哦，那个有效或无效”，你可以尝试一些新的东西或继续下去。这简直是​​无价之宝。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is really interesting that your answer wasn't like its outcome or some key results and 70% of success is goal, that there's something more fundamental, which is just being very clear on what you should be doing next week and we should be focusing on now. And that translates into what kind of the OKR process ends up being.
turns.zh: 这真的很有趣，你的答案不像它的结果或一些关键结果，70% 的成功是目标，还有一些更基本的东西，这只是非常清楚你下周应该做什么，我们现在应该关注。这转化为最终的 OKR 流程类型。

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Oh, yeah. Can I tell you a little story?
turns.zh: 哦，是的。我可以告诉你一个小故事吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 绝对地。

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: So, this is personal OKRs, but it works for everything else. It's always easier to talk about personal OKRs because I don't have to do an NDA with myself, so I apologize. But I've had this accountability group with these three women for at least five years, and every Monday we send our OKRs to each other, and I do it the way I do it in the book. Another woman, she had the getting things done approach where it was like, "How percentage did I make and what am I trying to do?" And exactly, super detailed. (00:14:06): And then another woman was like, "Ah, I don't know. I guess I'm trying to think about... What am I trying to think about? Oh, maybe I should think about if I have to get out of product management or not." Well, now the woman who was very precise has kind of disappeared. I think it was just something that she couldn't keep up that level of diligence. While the woman who was hand-waving, she actually has gone from a product manager to a consultant to a life coach, and she's making so much money, and she is so damn happy, and she has a new house. And so, I really do think that the heart of everything is answering that question.
turns.zh: 所以，这是个人 OKR，但它适用于其他一切。谈论个人 OKR 总是更容易，因为我不必与自己签订 NDA，所以我很抱歉。但我和这三位女性组成的问责小组已经至少五年了，每周一我们都会互相发送 OKR，我按照书中的方式去做。另一位女性，她的方法是把事情做好，就像是“我赚了多少百分比，我想做什么？”准确地说，非常详细。 (00:14:06)：然后另一个女人说，“啊，我不知道。我想我正在尝试思考......我在尝试思考什么？哦，也许我应该考虑是否必须退出产品管理。”好吧，现在那个非常精确的女人已经消失了。我认为这只是她无法保持那种勤奋程度的原因。那个挥手的女人，她实际上已经从产品经理变成了顾问，变成了生活教练，而且她赚了这么多钱，她太幸福了，而且她有了新房子。所以，我确实认为一切的核心都是回答这个问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And what is that question?
turns.zh: 那问题是什么？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: What am I doing this week to get to the outcome I really want? Her outcome was to not worry about money and be joyful with what she was doing. And she got that just by every Monday saying, "What the fuck am I doing here? What am I trying to do again?" And it worked.
turns.zh: 这周我要做什么才能达到我真正想要的结果？她的结果是不再担心金钱，并对自己所做的事情感到高兴。她每周一都会说：“我他妈的在这里做什么？我又想做什么？”它奏效了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is a really cool framework. So, the question you ask yourself every week is, "What am I doing today that's helping me get closer to my outcomes?" Is that the word to use outcome?
turns.zh: 这是一个非常酷的框架。因此，您每周都会问自己一个问题：“我今天在做什么可以帮助我更接近目标？”这是用结果这个词吗？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly. And it is an outcome. In her case, it was not worrying about money, having a house, having joy in her work. I think a lot of us get caught up in, do I want to be a writer? Do I want to be this thing? When the reality is, we just want to be satisfied and happy. And with a business, it's the same thing. We get caught up in this or that little details, but you need to go back and say, "What was our mission?" I mean, think about it. How often do companies ever talk about their mission? It's like they set it, they forget it, it's super vague, it's useless. (00:15:42): Instead, it's good to think, "Okay, when we started this company or when we changed this company or grew this company," or whatever you want to go to, there's always these various points in time. "Why? What did we think would work? And let's go back to that moment of meaning and reconnect with it and then make it real in the activities we take every week." And I like every week rather than every day. Because the reality is we still have to do progress reviews and we still have to do accounting and whatnot, but if we just push a little bit each week, over time amazing things happen.
turns.zh: 是的，是的，完全正确。这是一个结果。对她来说，不担心钱，拥有房子，享受工作的乐趣。我想我们很多人都会陷入这样的困境：我想成为一名作家吗？我想成为这样的人吗？当现实如此时，我们只想满足和快乐。对于企业来说，也是同样的事情。我们会陷入这样或那样的小细节中，但你需要回过头来说，“我们的使命是什么？”我的意思是，想一想。公司多久谈论一次他们的使命？就像他们设置了它，他们忘记了它，它非常模糊，毫无用处。 (00:15:42)：相反，最好这样想：“好吧，当我们创办这家公司时，或者当我们改变这家公司或发展这家公司时，”或者无论你想去哪里，总有这些不同的时间点。 “为什么？我们认为什么会起作用？让我们回到那个有意义的时刻并重新联系它，然后在我们每周进行的活动中将其变为现实。”我喜欢每周而不是每天。因为现实是我们仍然需要进行进度审查，我们仍然需要进行会计等等，但是如果我们每周稍微推动一点，随着时间的推移，惊人的事情就会发生。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, I want to drill into some of these things, of just how mission, vision, roadmap and OKRs kind of fit together, just to be pretty tactical. So, as a PM say, or founder, what is the process you recommend for working through mission, vision, and then OKRs, and then roadmap?
turns.zh: 因此，我想深入探讨其中的一些内容，即使命、愿景、路线图和 OKR 是如何结合在一起的，只是为了具有相当的战术性。那么，正如 PM 或创始人所说，您建议执行使命、愿景、OKR、路线图的流程是什么？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: I think it's really important to have a mission, and people get freaked out because they think the mission's forever. And so, they make them super vague so they can do anything. But instead, if you think about it, if the mission lasts for five years, what would you like to see happen in five years? And it might be, "We're going to bring amazing games that delight our users and we're proud to ship into the world." That could be a mission. And it's like, "Okay, I could do that over the next five years." And then, there'll be a point where you probably want to change again. So, you're bringing, what does it mean? What does it mean to be proud? What does it mean to delight people? Really talk about that and get into the nitty-gritty. And then out of that would come your strategy, which is this is going to be our year of exploration, if you have enough money for such a thing. (00:17:18): Or this is going to be our year of making our current games a little bit better. I'm in a very game mindset today because I was talking to a client. So, you get into that. Okay, now we have this sort of idea of what we're doing with our year. Now, let's talk about the quarter. And you can use OKRs for the year, but the quarter is where they have the most impact, I believe. Spotify talked about doing quarterly performance reviews because it's long enough to get something done and short enough to not forget what you did. And I think that sums it up perfectly for OKRs as well. So, once you know where you're trying to be, and once you know what you want to do with your year, you can say, "What are the things we want to see happen across these four quarters?" (00:18:01): I call it sort of a half-built strategy because too much strategy ties you down and too little strategy, you're too responsive to everything. So, you say, "Okay." Let's say you're building a new game. So, Q1 is about figuring out what it is and what's going to be interesting to users. And then Q2 is going to be about getting some early prototypes out and validating those concepts. And Q3 is about building extensive, and Q4 is about marketing and throwing it out, something like that. And you could venture them into your outcomes. A lot of people who are very venture driven don't understand outcomes, objectives, excuse me, objectives, outcomes, potato, potato.
turns.zh: 我认为有使命真的很重要，人们会感到害怕，因为他们认为使命是永远的。因此，他们让他们变得非常模糊，这样他们就可以做任何事情。但相反，如果你想一想，如果任务持续五年，你希望看到五年后发生什么？它可能是，“我们将带来令人惊叹的游戏，让我们的用户感到高兴，我们很自豪能够将其推向世界。”这可能是一个使命。就像，“好吧，我可以在未来五年内做到这一点。”然后，到了某个时刻你可能想再次改变。那么，你带来了，这意味着什么？骄傲是什么意思？使人高兴是什么意思？真正谈论这一点并进入实质内容。然后你的策略就会随之而来，如果你有足够的资金来做这样的事情，这将是我们探索的一年。 (00:17:18)：或者说，今年将是我们让当前游戏变得更好的一年。今天我处于一种非常游戏的心态，因为我正在与客户交谈。所以，你开始吧。好的，现在我们对这一年要做的事情有了这样的想法。现在，我们来谈谈本季度的情况。您可以在全年使用 OKR，但我相信季度是它们影响最大的地方。 Spotify 谈到进行季度绩效评估，因为它足够长，可以完成某件事，也足够短，可以让你不会忘记你所做的事情。我认为这也完美地概括了 OKR。因此，一旦您知道自己想要达到的目标，并且知道这一年想要做什么，您就可以说：“我们希望看到这四个季度发生哪些事情？” (00:18:01)：我称其为半成品策略，因为太多的策略会束缚你，而太少的策略会让你对一切都过于敏感。所以，你说：“好吧。”假设您正在开发一款新游戏。因此，第一季度是要弄清楚它是什么以及用户会感兴趣什么。然后第二季度将推出一些早期原型并验证这些概念。第三季度是关于广泛建设，第四季度是关于营销和抛弃，类似的事情。你可以将它们投入到你的成果中。很多非常热衷于风险投资的人不理解结果、目标，对不起，目标、结果，土豆，土豆。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And they sound horrid.
turns.zh: 它们听起来很可怕。

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: It's really something inspiring. Q1, we have a vision for this game that will drive us forward. I don't know, I'm making stuff up, which just means it's going to be imperfect. Although I do warn people not to get too caught up in wordsmithing. We can spend hours doing that. And then, you get to ask my favorite question, how do we know? I love, how do we know? That's how you get to outcomes. So, what does it mean to have a vision for a product we believe will be successful and meet our mission, whatnot? Well, what would it be? How are we going to figure this out? So, something about user testing, probably. Maybe we do a landing page, see how many people are excited by the concept. Maybe we do some technical builds to see if it's actually buildable. What are the sort of things that would tell us, yes, please go forward? We might be excited about VR. Well, how do we know that VR would be profitable for us? (00:19:35): So, once we answer those three, how would we know, then we can know that by March we have the results we need. And we're always going to try to think about the best possible future, the whole moonshot thing, which I'm a fan of, but the reality is, the reason we do that estimating is so we get good at estimating. Everybody sucks at estimating when you first start, and a lot of people think it's like black magic or something you're born with. But no, it's a learned skill. You practice estimating, you get good at estimating, you get better and better and better. And being good at estimating is incredibly valuable as a business skill. So, there's your OKRs, right? And then for Q2, we don't know how Q1 is going to go, so we're just going to leave the objective there, but we're not going to get into the nitty-gritty OKRs. Key results cause a lot of arguing among the team, takes forever to track them down, just wait and see how Q1 goes. And that way you have enough play within your strategy to react to new information.
turns.zh: 这确实是一件鼓舞人心的事情。 Q1，我们对这款游戏有一个愿景，它将推动我们前进。我不知道，我正在编造一些东西，这只是意味着它会不完美。尽管我确实警告人们不要太沉迷于文字创作。我们可以花几个小时来做​​这件事。然后，你可以问我最喜欢的问题，我们怎么知道？我爱，我们怎么知道？这就是你获得结果的方式。那么，拥有一个我们相信会成功并实现我们使命的产品愿景意味着什么？嗯，那会是什么？我们该如何解决这个问题？那么，可能是关于用户测试的一些事情。也许我们做一个登陆页面，看看有多少人对这个概念感到兴奋。也许我们会做一些技术构建来看看它是否真的可以构建。什么样的事情会告诉我们“是的，请继续”？我们可能会对 VR 感到兴奋。那么，我们怎么知道 VR 会给我们带来利润呢？ (00:19:35)：所以，一旦我们回答了这三个问题，我们如何知道，然后我们就可以知道到三月份我们会得到我们需要的结果。我们总是会尝试思考最好的未来，整个登月计划，我是它的粉丝，但现实是，我们进行估算的原因是为了让我们擅长估算。当你刚开始的时候，每个人都不擅长估计，而且很多人认为这就像黑魔法或你与生俱来的东西。但不，这是一项习得的技能。你练习估算，你会擅长估算，你会变得越来越好。善于估计作为一项商业技能非常有价值。那么，这就是您的 OKR，对吗？然后对于第二季度，我们不知道第一季度将如何进行，因此我们将把目标留在那里，但我们不会深入讨论 OKR 的细节。关键结果会在团队中引起很多争论，需要很长时间才能找到它们，只需等待，看看第一季度进展如何。这样你就可以在策略中发挥足够的作用来对新信息做出反应。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The question you talked about of, how do we know? That's to decide the objective or the key results?
turns.zh: 你提到的问题，我们怎么知道？那是决定目标还是关键结果？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Key results, yeah.
turns.zh: 关键结果，是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, got it. You're saying objective. Okay, cool.
turns.zh: 好的，明白了。你说的是客观的。好吧，酷。

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Objective. My bad. I didn't signal when I turned. No.
turns.zh: 客观的。我的不好。我转身时没有打手势。不。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, okay, cool. That makes sense.
turns.zh: 哦，好吧，酷。这是有道理的。

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Objective is that vision for the quarter. This is what we're we're driving towards in this quarter. And then the key results, you answered the question, how do we know we succeeded?
turns.zh: 目标是本季度的愿景。这就是我们本季度的目标。然后是关键结果，你回答了这个问题，我们如何知道我们成功了？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so, what was the tip you gave of turning strategy into the objective? How do you translate from strategy to deciding your objective for the core?
turns.zh: 那么，您给出的将战略转化为目标的建议是什么？您如何从战略转变为确定核心目标？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Oh, that sits between mission and OKRs. So, strategy, I've been really shocked lately. I've discovered that lots of companies don't seem to have any strategy whatsoever, which just blows my mind. So, if you think about strategy as a strongly held hypothesis about a way to win in the market and fulfill our vision, then you can say, "Well, our mission is this, or vision..." I kind of use them interchangeably because I think they are kind of interchangeable, and I'm not going to get in semantics in the bitty bits, but the strategy is really important because it says, "We think we're fulfilling our mission of connecting people, by what?" (00:21:55): I think that there are a lot of good product strategy pieces out there, but businesses have a lot of questions to answer. Are we going to ship physical products? Are we going to ship digital products? Are we going to be a service? Are we going to do a subscription? Strategy answers those questions. They say, "We're going to have a game. It's going to be an Apple Arcade. We have a hypothesis that's actually going to help us. We're going to build in there and build our customer base there in order to get name recognition, which we can then use on other platforms." That's the sort of strategic stuff. And then we're like, "Oh great, you have a vision. What are we doing? What does that actually mean for us this year, this quarter, and then eventually this week?"
turns.zh: 哦，这介于使命和 OKR 之间。所以，策略，我最近真的很震惊。我发现很多公司似乎没有任何战略，这让我大吃一惊。因此，如果你将战略视为一种关于赢得市场并实现我们愿景的强烈假设，那么你可以说，“嗯，我们的使命是这个，或者愿景……”我可以互换使用它们，因为我认为它们是可以互换的，而且我不会深入讨论语义，但战略非常重要，因为它说，“我们认为我们正在通过什么来实现连接人们的使命？” (00:21:55)：我认为有很多好的产品策略，但企业有很多问题需要回答。我们要运送实物产品吗？我们要运送数字产品吗？我们要做服务吗？我们要订阅吗？战略回答了这些问题。他们说，“我们将推出一款游戏。它将成为 Apple Arcade。我们有一个实际上对我们有帮助的假设。我们将在那里构建并建立我们的客户群，以获得知名度，然后我们可以在其他平台上使用它。”这就是战略性的东西。然后我们会说，“哦，太棒了，你有一个愿景。我们在做什么？这对我们今年、本季度以及最终本周实际上意味着什么？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For the actual OKRs you end up with, is it as simple as just with the template of an OKR, is it just objective three-ish key results? Is there anything more to it that you recommend folks use?
turns.zh: 对于最终得到的实际 OKR，是不是像 OKR 模板一样简单，只是客观的三个关键结果？您还有什么建议人们使用的吗？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: No. Simple things give you a lot more room to fiddle. And I feel like every time I see people make really complicated methodologies, they get way too caught up in the rules and they don't think about, what are we actually trying to do? So, simple is better.
turns.zh: 不会。简单的事情会给你更多的发挥空间。我觉得每次我看到人们制定非常复杂的方法时，他们都过于拘泥于规则，而没有思考，我们实际上想做什么？所以，简单更好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And what's your rule of thumb for number of key results?
turns.zh: 您对关键结果数量的经验法则是什么？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: I like three. I think about it as triangulating. I always like something that's really hardcore numbers. I like something that's a little squishier, like a quality, make sure you don't forget about it. And I usually like something that involves a dollar sign, but it's really going to be specific to what objective you're trying to do. Launch a new product. Well, you probably want to make a certain amount of money, well you want a certain amount of reach, and then you want that delight thing. And then when you get into the delight thing, you can say, "Well, is it going to be Metacritic? Is it going to be a survey? Is it going to be NPS?" You know, could figure out what one makes the most sense for you.
turns.zh: 我喜欢三个。我认为这是三角测量。我总是喜欢一些真正硬核的数字。我喜欢稍微软一点的东西，比如品质，确保你不要忘记它。我通常喜欢涉及美元符号的东西，但它实际上是针对你想要实现的目标的。推出新产品。好吧，你可能想赚一定数量的钱，你想要一定程度的影响力，然后你想要那种令人愉悦的东西。然后当你进入令人高兴的事情时，你可以说，“嗯，它会是 Metacritic？它会是一项调查吗？它会是 NPS 吗？”你知道，可以找出对你来说最有意义的一个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's an interesting topic. Is there anything you find there to measure customer happiness, satisfaction, delight? What have you seen work best for that sort of squishy stuff?
turns.zh: 这是一个有趣的话题。您发现有什么可以衡量客户的幸福感、满意度和愉悦感吗？你见过什么最适合这种软乎乎的东西？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: I know there's a big backlash against NPS. I think it's okay. It's really funny because you can be insanely successful with a game that people feel yucky to play, and you can be incredibly successful with a product people hate using. Zoom, for example. How many times have you heard Zoom get cussed out? So, the question is, why would I care about that if I'm making money? And I would say the answer is, would you like to keep making money? It's always about retention.
turns.zh: 我知道人们对 NPS 有很大的反对。我觉得还可以。这真的很有趣，因为你可以通过一款人们觉得难玩的游戏取得疯狂的成功，而你可以通过一款人们讨厌使用的产品取得令人难以置信的成功。例如，缩放。您听过多少次 Zoom 被骂？那么问题来了，如果我能赚钱，为什么还要关心这个呢？我想说的答案是，你想继续赚钱吗？这始终与保留有关。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 正确的。

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: So, anytime you can get strong retention signals, I think those are good signals to get. So, that comes out of qualitative research. There's nothing better. So, if you don't have a qualitative researcher on your team, I think you should get one. You need somebody who knows how to separate what people say and what they do, and what the truth is in that. And then use that to apply to your strategic decisions, so that happy users sell your product for you, right? Happy users stay with your product. Happy users are willing to type an email telling you when you're messing up. I mean, you want committed users. They're just so important.
turns.zh: 因此，只要你能获得强烈的保留信号，我认为这些都是很好的信号。所以，这是来自定性研究。没有什么比这更好的了。因此，如果您的团队中没有定性研究员，我认为您应该找一位。你需要一个知道如何区分人们所说和所做的事情以及其中的真相的人。然后将其应用于您的战略决策，以便满意的用户为您销售您的产品，对吧？快乐的用户会继续使用你的产品。当您遇到麻烦时，快乐的用户愿意输入电子邮件告诉您。我的意思是，你需要忠诚的用户。它们是如此重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: One final question around the actual OKR document. What do you find are the most one or two common mistakes people make when writing out the objective or the key result in deciding on what to go with?
turns.zh: 关于实际 OKR 文档的最后一个问题。您发现人们在写出目标或决定如何选择的关键结果时最常犯的一两个错误是什么？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Objectives, people make them so fluffy that they don't have any meaning. They really should be a proper goal. We're doing this because we want to see this happen, it matters. We want to delight our customers. Sometimes people make them too fluffy and sometimes they make them too boring. It's like, "Oh, we're going to ship this thing." That doesn't inspire anybody. Your objectives should make you, when your alarm goes off and you wake up, you go, "Oh yeah, I'm changing the world today, or I'm doing something really cool." It shouldn't be like, snooze. So, I think an objective should be motivating but not ridiculous. (00:25:42): And then the key results, it's always going to be tasks. I mean, people put tasks in there all the time, and it can be tricky. Sometimes it feels like a task, like you have to get past a product review, so it's going to have a binary. They either said yes or no. But when you think about it, it is an outcome because it's really hard to get a product review group to say okay to anything. So, making sure that you have real outcomes that let you move forward, I think that's the biggest mistake people make in OKRs.
turns.zh: 目标，人们把它们弄得很空洞，没有任何意义。它们确实应该是一个正确的目标。我们这样做是因为我们希望看到这种情况发生，这很重要。我们希望让我们的客户满意。有时人们把它们做得太蓬松，有时又把它们做得太无聊。就像，“哦，我们要运送这个东西。”这不会激励任何人。你的目标应该让你，当你的闹钟响起，你醒来时，你会说，“哦，是的，我今天正在改变世界，或者我正在做一些非常酷的事情。”不应该是这样，打瞌睡。所以，我认为目标应该是激励性的，而不是荒谬的。 (00:25:42)：然后是关键结果，它总是任务。我的意思是，人们总是把任务放在那里，这可能很棘手。有时感觉像是一项任务，就像你必须通过产品审查，所以它将有一个二进制文件。他们要么说是，要么说不是。但当你仔细想想，这只是一个结果，因为让产品审查小组对任何事情说“好”真的很难。因此，确保你有真正的成果让你前进，我认为这是人们在 OKR 中犯的最大错误。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. I know you shared a few examples of just that came top-of-mind, but just is there any examples you can think of just, here's a really good example of an outcome? And I think your results are a lot easier, just move this metric 10% or hit-
turns.zh: 是的。我知道您分享了一些最重要的例子，但是您是否能想到一些例子，这是一个非常好的结果示例？我认为你的结果要容易得多，只需将该指标移动 10% 或点击-

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Let's try to keep it fairly concrete. You're a online magazine selling interior design ideas. So, what are you trying to do? You're trying to get strong leads out to your advertisers, and that's really important, and you're doing it because you believe that people deserve to have homes that are warm and wonderful. You have this mission, and you want to make money while you do it. So, your strategy is going to be about connecting human beings with the brands that will suit their lifestyle. Okay, that's great. And then we get to the nitty-gritty, well, what does that actually mean? Are we going to really work on recommendations passionately? Are we going to really create various markets and throw down advertising where we think these people are? That's when your strategy comes into play because you're making all these interesting choices. So, let's say we're going to double down on recommendations, which has a lot of presuppositions. (00:27:23): We have to get people to like, we have to understand their patterns of behavior, and that's when we can start to go to OKRs. We can say, "Okay, so we have this online magazine, let's really work to get as many people being members rather than browsers as possible, so that we can start understanding what they like." And that's what Q1 could be really about, is starting to collect profiles of people's passions, and that sounds kind of exciting. "Okay, great. We're going to do that. We're going to create a profile of people's passions. Awesome." So, how would we know we were successful? "Oh, gosh. Well, we probably need a bunch of people to do it, but do we really need everybody? Maybe 30% of our audience flips over, and maybe that's right, maybe that's wrong." If you don't know, you just set it and you'll know by the end of Q3, whether you were stupid or not, it's fine, move on. (00:28:12): Okay, that's great. Okay, how many things should people do what with? So, they bookmark, favorite, like... How about like? Okay, so maybe they're going to like a certain number of products each week. Let's go for weekly active users. So, they're going to like three things and present it. Okay, so now we've got a couple of numbers that are pretty good. How do we know they're actually kind of liking it? Maybe you decide to do some panels, and we're going to measure using a customer panel, bring them in, have them talk to us, and we're going to do that at the end of every two weeks to hear how it's working and understand more about it. (00:28:54): Okay, now we have some OKRs. With key results, I always recommend spending 10 minutes brainstorming every single way you could possibly measure that outcome. Because with brainstorms, you always think of all the obvious stuff first and then you have no ideas and you're just sitting there with your post notes going, "How long is 10 minutes anyway?" And then you start getting the weird ideas. And often out of those weird ideas are really good insights. So, I recommend some pretty long brainstormings on the key results, but the objective is sort of a manifestation of the strategy at a one quarter level.
turns.zh: 让我们尽量保持它相当具体。您是一本销售室内设计理念的在线杂志。那么，你想做什么？你正在努力为你的广告商带来强有力的线索，这非常重要，你这样做是因为你相信人们应该拥有温暖而美好的家。你有这个使命，你想在执行的同时赚钱。因此，您的策略是将人类与适合他们生活方式的品牌联系起来。好的，太好了。然后我们开始讨论本质，这到底意味着什么？我们真的会热情地致力于推荐工作吗？我们真的要创造各种市场并在我们认为这些人所在的地方投放广告吗？这就是你的策略发挥作用的时候，因为你正在做出所有这些有趣的选择。因此，假设我们要加倍努力提出建议，其中有很多假设。 (00:27:23)：我们必须让人们喜欢，我们必须了解他们的行为模式，然后我们就可以开始实行 OKR。我们可以说：“好吧，我们有了这本在线杂志，让我们努力让尽可能多的人成为会员而不是浏览者，这样我们就可以开始了解他们喜欢什么。”这就是第一季度的真正目的，开始收集人们的热情概况，这听起来有点令人兴奋。 “好吧，太好了。我们将这样做。我们将创建一个关于人们热情的档案。太棒了。”那么，我们怎么知道我们成功了呢？ “哦，天哪。好吧，我们可能需要一群人来做这件事，但我们真的需要每个人吗？也许 30% 的观众会翻脸，也许这是对的，也许是错的。”如果你不知道，你就设置它，到第三季度结束时你就会知道，无论你是否愚蠢，都没关系，继续前进。 (00:28:12)：好的，太好了。好吧，人们应该用多少东西来做呢？所以，他们添加书签、收藏、喜欢……喜欢怎么样？好吧，也许他们每周会喜欢一定数量的产品。我们来看看每周的活跃用户。所以，他们会喜欢三样东西并展示它。好的，现在我们得到了一些相当不错的数字。我们怎么知道他们真的喜欢它？也许您决定做一些面板，我们将使用客户面板进行测量，让他们进来，让他们与我们交谈，我们将每两周结束时这样做，以了解其工作原理并了解更多信息。 (00:28:54)：好的，现在我们有了一些 OKR。对于关键结果，我始终建议您花 10 分钟集思广益，对可能衡量该结果的每一种方法进行头脑风暴。因为在头脑风暴中，你总是先想到所有显而易见的东西，然后你就没有任何想法，你只是坐在那里，在你的帖子上写着“10 分钟到底有多长？”然后你开始产生奇怪的想法。这些奇怪的想法往往会产生非常好的见解。因此，我建议对关键结果进行一些相当长的头脑风暴，但目标是四分之一级别的战略体现。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. That was an awesome example. You talked a bit earlier about how OKRs end up being... or sorry, key results end up being tasks for a lot of people. And this reminds me, we had the CPO of Figma on this podcast, and he told the story of how they moved away from OKRs at one point because they found themselves sitting in these meetings reviewing these large spreadsheets of hundreds of tasks-
turns.zh: 惊人的。这是一个很棒的例子。您之前谈到过 OKR 最终如何……或者抱歉，关键结果最终成为很多人的任务。这让我想起，我们在这个播客中邀请了 Figma 的 CPO，他讲述了他们如何一度放弃 OKR 的故事，因为他们发现自己坐在这些会议中审查这些包含数百项任务的大型电子表格 -

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: Oh, god. Yeah.
turns.zh: 哦，上帝。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... that were basically just tasks for ICs that they're working on, and they kind of lost sight of why does any of this matter? What are you even trying to do as a company? So, they moved away from OKRs and then they came back to them actually later and fixing some of these issues. So, maybe just as a question, what do you think is a sign that your OKR process is busted and that you need to spend some time improving and rethinking the way it works?
turns.zh: ...这基本上只是他们正在研究的 IC 的任务，他们有点忽视了为什么这很重要？作为一家公司，你到底想做什么？因此，他们放弃了 OKR，然后又回到 OKR 并解决了其中一些问题。那么，也许只是作为一个问题，您认为什么迹象表明您的 OKR 流程已被破坏，并且您需要花一些时间改进和重新思考其工作方式？

turns.speaker: Christina Wodtke
turns.en: I think if those meetings are boring, that's a great example. One of the other benefits, which I didn't bring up about OKRs is that they scale really well. One of the biggest problems founders struggle with is they don't scale very well, but if you can set a good OKR and get people to work on it, then you don't have to decide all those little IC tasks. You don't want to be drug down with that. You got a job. CEOs got to figure out what's coming up down the line, not fiddling over everybody's tasks. So, you set the OKRs and then you ask in the meeting, "What are the top three initiatives that you're doing towards them?" Or two or five, whatever. It's going to vary a little bit, but you want to keep it small. You only want to look at the most important stuff and just trust your people to take care of everything else. (00:30:58): And then you can say, "Well, why do you think that's important? What do you think that's going to do?" Or, "I've been seeing that for weeks. Are you going to try something else anytime soon?" It's all about those conversations about, is our current strategy, not just at the company level, but at each departmental level, are these strategies working? Are they moving us forward, towards our goals? And so, looking through OKRs, I tell people, "When you first start, it might take a half hour, but after that it should just take 10 minutes." It's like, "I think that's stupid. We should talk about that." Or, "No, it looks fine, looks essentially correct, let's move on. Anybody got anything?" And then you can get into whatever else you do, if it's a metrics review situation or if it's talking about a new deal, the rest of the agenda. (00:31:43): But that constant checking in is like touching a lucky stone in your pocket. It reminds you, "Oh yeah, there's this thing, there's this thing." And that rhythm... I'm a teacher, I'm really into learning theory. So, there's a really big concept which is about repetition and retrieval practice. So, retrieval practice means that I put a fact in your brain and I keep asking you to go back and get it again. Qualitative research is really useful for understanding the psychology of your users. (00:32:15): I'll say, "Well, how do we understand the psychology of users?" And you'd be like, "Oh, I heard this." Okay, I bring it up. Well, it's the same thing in these weekly meetings, you're practicing retrieving what your OKRs are, and after a while they're just in that long-term memory and you don't have to struggle to think about them and you've got them. And anytime you make a decision and you're in a big rush, you don't want to go through a bunch of paper to try to find what were our OKRs? You just go, "Boo, this is what we should do. I know what we're trying to do and I know how to make a decision about that."
turns.zh: 我认为如果这些会议很无聊，那就是一个很好的例子。我没有提到 OKR 的其他好处之一是它们的扩展性非常好。创始人面临的最大问题之一是他们不能很好地扩展，但如果你可以设定一个好的 OKR 并让人们致力于它，那么你就不必决定所有这些小 IC 任务。你不想因此而吸毒。你找到工作了。首席执行官们必须弄清楚接下来会发生什么，而不是摆弄每个人的任务。因此，您设定 OKR，然后在会议中询问：“您针对 OKR 采取的最重要的三项举措是什么？”或者两个或五个，无论如何。它会略有不同，但您希望保持较小。您只想关注最重要的事情，并相信您的员工会处理其他所有事情。 (00:30:58)：然后你可以说，“好吧，为什么你认为这很重要？你认为这会做什么？”或者，“我已经看到这种情况好几个星期了。你打算很快尝试其他东西吗？”这一切都与这些对话有关，我们当前的策略，不仅在公司层面，而且在每个部门层面，这些策略是否有效？他们是否正在推动我们前进，实现我们的目标？因此，在查看 OKR 时，我告诉人们，“刚开始时，可​​能需要半小时，但之后应该只需要 10 分钟。”就像，“我认为这很愚蠢。我们应该谈谈这个。”或者，“不，看起来不错，看起来基本正确，让我们继续吧。有人知道什么吗？”然后你就可以开始做任何其他事情，无论是指标审查情况还是谈论新交易，以及议程的其余部分。 (00:31:43)：但是不断地查看就像摸口袋里的幸运石一样。它提醒你，“哦，是的，有这个东西，有这个东西。”那种节奏……我是一名老师，我真的很喜欢学习理论。所以，有一个非常大的概念，那就是重复和检索练习。因此，检索练习意味着我将一个事实放入你的大脑中，并且不断要求你返回并再次获取它。定性研究对于了解用户的心理非常有用。 (00:32:15)：我会说，“那么，我们如何理解用户的心理呢？”你会说，“哦，我听到了这个。”好吧，我提出来。嗯，在这些每周的会议中也是一样的，你正在练习检索你的 OKR 是什么，过了一段时间，它们就进入了长期记忆，你不必费力去思考它们，你就已经得到了它们。每当你做出决定并且很匆忙时，你不想翻阅一堆文件来试图找出我们的 OKR 是什么？你只需说：“嘘，这就是我们应该做的。我知道我们要做什么，我知道如何做出决定。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, what I'm hearing is, a lot of this comes back to, if the meeting is not interesting and boring, change the way you run the meeting. Don't go through everything. Maybe just pick the things that are most interesting and focus on that. You don't have to review every single key result.
